The stability of each sorbent was evaluated by rapid aging, which was performed in the screening reactor. Typically, 0.5 g of sample was analyzed using real air and rapid adsorption/desorption cycles. Adsorption was performed under a flow of dried, real ambient air humidified to >90% RH for 15 minutes at a sample temperature of 28°C. This resulted in uptake of CO to partial capture capacity. Then, under the 2 same air flow, the sample was heated to the target desorption temperature and held for 20 minutes to allow for CO desorption. The sample was allowed to cool in humidified N to the target adsorption temperature 2 2 before the cycle was repeated. In the case of ECCOsorb-E2, the sample was aged rapidly in a drying oven (stagnant air) at 100°C, which is estimated to be equivalent to about 370 fast cycles. At the completion of the aging experiment, each sample was tested again under the standard conditions. Fresh ECCOsorb-1 showed the highest adsorption capacity of 1.82 mmol CO /g sorbent, followed by ECCOsorb-T1, 2 ECCOsorb-E1, and ECCOsorb-E2. Among the candidate samples, ECCOSorb-T1 demonstrated the highest capacity retention, particularly after enduring a more rigorous aging test.
